subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me a 6-mark exam-style question on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Why did it take a long time for Darwin's theory to be widely accepted?
options: It conflicted with religious beliefs and the mechanism of inheritance was not yet known
No one was interested in biology
questions.explain: Darwin's theory challenged religious views and lacked a known mechanism of inheritance (genes were not yet understood).

questions.q: Which of these is a NON-specific first line of defence against pathogens?
options: The skin acting as a barrier
questions.explain: The skin is a physical barrier that is non-specific, stopping pathogens entering before the immune response.

questions.q: Why does a vaccinated person respond faster if they later meet the real pathogen?
options: Memory cells remain and quickly produce antibodies
questions.explain: Vaccination leaves memory cells that rapidly produce the correct antibodies on re-exposure.

questions.q: Gonorrhoea is a sexually transmitted disease caused by a bacterium. How can its spread be controlled?
questions.explain: Gonorrhoea is treated with antibiotics, and barrier methods such as condoms reduce its spread.

questions.q: Salmonella food poisoning is caused by:
options: Bacteria spread in unhygienically prepared food
questions.explain: Salmonella bacteria are spread in food prepared in unhygienic conditions and produce toxins.

questions.q: Why are antibiotics useless against the common cold?
options: The cold virus is resistant to all drugs
Colds are caused by viruses, and antibiotics only kill bacteria
questions.explain: Antibiotics kill bacteria but cannot kill viruses, which reproduce inside the body's own cells.

questions.q: Which of these provides direct evidence for evolution?
options: Fossils showing how organisms have changed over time
questions.explain: Fossils show how species have gradually changed over millions of years, providing evidence for evolution.

questions.q: Which of these is a key part of natural selection?
options: Characteristics changing only within one lifetime
All organisms in a species being identical
Individuals with advantageous variations are more likely to survive and reproduce
Organisms choosing to change to suit their environment
questions.explain: In natural selection, individuals with advantageous inherited variations survive, reproduce and pass on those alleles.

questions.q: What is the word equation for photosynthesis?
questions.explain: Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide and water with light energy to make glucose and oxygen.

questions.q: The three-domain system, proposed by Carl Woese, divides life into:
questions.explain: Woese used genetic analysis to propose three domains: Archaea, Bacteria and Eukaryota.

questions.q: What is the gas produced by photosynthesis?
questions.explain: Oxygen is released as a product of photosynthesis.

questions.q: The rapid emergence of antibiotic-resistant bacteria is evidence for evolution because:
options: Resistant bacteria survive antibiotics and reproduce, so resistance spreads
Antibiotics create resistant bacteria from nothing
questions.explain: Resistant bacteria survive and reproduce by natural selection, demonstrating evolution happening quickly.
